sample_unit: benchmark items (30 NOHARM v2 public cases)
models_evaluated: 12 unnamed language models in total, 5 of them also tested with a structured instruction

links.outcome: Severity-weighted F1 with versus without a structured instruction requesting a complete plan
links.effect: Instruction raised F1 by 0.14 on average [0.09, 0.20] and improved 4 of 5 models. Between-model SD halved (0.17 to 0.09). One model added harmful options (+0.13 per item).
links.quote: The instruction raised F1 by 0.14 on average [0.09, 0.20] and improved 4 of 5 models, most for the tersest (Grok 4.7, 0.354 to 0.633; GPT-5.6 Terra, 0.678 to 0.853).

links.outcome: Dependence of benchmark scores on prompt configuration rather than model knowledge
links.effect: Three instructed models exceeded the best uninstructed score (0.764). Between-model SD fell from 0.17 to 0.09, so uninstructed rankings partly reflect how much a model volunteers.
links.quote: On this benchmark, an uninstructed score reflects how much a model volunteers, not only what it knows.

unlisted_practices: Reporting benchmark scores under a standard structured instruction alongside uninstructed scores
Checking what a structured instruction adds, including harmful options, before ranking models

screen.practice: structured prompt instruction requesting complete plan (prompt guardrail) with review of added actions
screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluation measuring the safety and completeness impact of a prompt engineering/instruction practice compared to uninstructed prompting on clinical consult cases.
